chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Ziyad al-Nahdi, from 'Abdullah ibn Wahb, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:
It is enough of a victory from God for the believer to see his enemy committing acts of disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.حسب: Sufficient, enough — indicates that divine support takes many forms
key_terms.معاصي: Sins, acts of disobedience against God's commands
key_terms.نصرة: Victory, divine support — God's aid for the believer

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the believer and their enemy?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that a true believer needs no worldly retaliation against his enemies, for the greatest divine support is witnessing one's adversary engaged in sin against God. This teaching was delivered in the context of encouraging believers to maintain moral composure when wronged, reminding them that an enemy's sinfulness is itself a sign of their own spiritual defeat.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Ibn Abi `Umayr from Abi Ziyad al-Nahdi from `Abdullah b. Wahab from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as).
He said: For a believer, it is enough of a victory from Allah to see his enemy disobeying Allah.
